summary: Blue Ridge Audubon is a chapter of the National Audubon Society serving Buncombe, Henderson, and surrounding WNC counties, run as a volunteer-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a board of directors, members, free program meetings, monthly bird outings, and sanctuary workdays. The listed event itself is a Swannanoa Valley Museum program ('History is for the Birds', $65, biweekly) merely led by a guide supplied by the chapter, not the chapter's own membership activity, but the chapter behind that guide is a genuine returning-member organization.

evidence.note: Listing is a museum-run bird-walk series at the Swannanoa Valley Museum & History Center, priced at $65, each session 'led by an experienced guide from the Blue Ridge Audubon Chapter' rather than run by the chapter itself.

Chapter homepage confirms it is a National Audubon Society chapter with a board of directors, members, free program meetings with guest speakers, monthly bird outings at Beaver Lake Bird Sanctuary and Jackson Park, and Tuesday habitat-restoration workdays.

Chapter is currently running a named capital campaign (Beaver Lake Bird Sanctuary Renewal Project, $100,000 goal), indicating an active, organized, returning volunteer base rather than a one-off event.
